transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

At work my mind jumps to every little thing going on around me, and I lose track of what I’m doing in the middle of a customer call. It has gotten to the point where it's really affecting my ability to do my job.
Have you experienced these difficulties with concentration and staying on task since you were a child, or is this a more recent change in your life?

Actually, it goes all the way back to elementary school; my teachers used to move my seat because I was always talking, tapping my pencil, or staring out the window. My report cards always said I was smart but "didn't pay attention" and made careless mistakes. However, it has really come to a head and gotten much worse over the last two years since my job switched to a new, fast-paced tracking system.
Do you find that your inability to concentrate is primarily driven by feeling overwhelmed and worried about your job performance, or does your mind wander even when you are not feeling anxious?

The stress at work definitely makes things feel worse, but my mind has always wandered even when I'm completely calm. Since I was a kid, my brain would just drift off or get pulled away by random thoughts, even during simple, quiet moments when there is nothing to worry about.
Do you often feel like you are driven by a motor, or do you frequently find yourself interrupting others or struggling to wait your turn during conversations?

Yes, my family actually jokes that I'm like a wind-up toy because I'm constantly bouncing from one thing to the next and can't seem to rest. I also struggle a lot with interrupting people and finishing their sentences because my thoughts just pop out before I can stop them. Waiting my turn, whether on team calls or standing in lines, makes me feel so incredibly antsy that I often end up cutting in.
